source.proofMethod: Compile-only proof: compileGameplayModuleGraph with the full registry plus typed proof fixtures; every emitted registry descriptor is checked through authorModuleUi(...).authoring === standard. Runtime result equivalence is reported separately by output/completion-compatibility-behavior-proof.json.

proofs.equivalence: The public cell occupancy field is authoritative for live occupancy; negating it reproduces the empty-cell boolean without the retired cell-equal or compare.equal adapters.

A one-based collection.at over the typed choice sequence reads x/y through the public record field and reconstructs the cell. Valid cell choices retain the first-item semantics; malformed choice records remain host-invalid rather than gaining an author guard.
The first choice record supplies the pieceId, and a public query/find over live piece handles resolves the matching instance without the retired piece-identifier adapter.
The public owner/relation/liveness query is the host policy boundary for the affectable set; no local compatibility predicate or retired alive adapter is needed.
proofs.hostBoundary: Host query.pieces retains relation and living-target policy; this proof does not replace that host policy with a text or owner comparison.

proofs.equivalence: The public enemy query is filtered by x/y coordinate comparison against the supplied cells. The outer piece query order is retained while cell membership uses a bounded find.

The public graph iterates the supplied cells in order, filters candidates at each cell, removes duplicate instanceIds, and concatenates in encounter order. It does not sort or replace the ordered-cell traversal.
A public live-piece query followed by instanceId field comparison and one-based find resolves the same nullable piece handle for an existing identifier.
The identifier alias has the same public instanceId lookup composition; the input name remains a graph-local compatibility spelling and does not add a module.

Public board cells are bounded by coordinate comparisons, then resolved one cell at a time through a public find and concatenated. The fixed board-cell traversal preserves the legacy x/y rectangle order for the validated bounded rectangle.
The all-relation variant uses the same public cell-membership filter over the live piece query; no retired cell-equal module is required.
A typed cell is read and reconstructed with public coordinate/constructor primitives. Null/presence propagation remains an engine input boundary and is not exposed as a separate author guard.
The public live-piece filter compares both position and instanceId, so the authenticated ignored piece is excluded before the count-to-zero test.
The public cell occupancy field and boolean negation provide the no-ignore form; null-cell handling is left to the typed host boundary.
The public cell field reads walkability for a valid optional cell; nullable absence is propagated by the compiler/host input boundary rather than an author-facing present-cell adapter.
The public cell field is the direct walkability read; no retired present-cell or cell-walkable descriptor is used.

The public map-cell set is used only as the membership authority while the outer filter preserves caller order; each retained item is then rebuilt from pure x/y coordinates so decorated input fields cannot change the canonical cell result.

notes: These are bounded public graph compilation proofs only. They do not claim runtime result equivalence; the paired execution comparison is in output/completion-compatibility-behavior-proof.json.
compare.equal/compare.equal-string/cell-equal/piece.identifier are replaced by compare.values, coordinate fields, and piece.field(instanceId).
Collection.filter/reduce/find emit ordered array traversal; ordered-cell proofs retain the caller sequence and deduplicate only by the old instanceId rule.
cell-require/present-cell and finite-number checks remain host/type propagation boundaries, not gameplay author guards.
